Before rivers learned to run, the world was a bowl of dust beneath a silent sky. In those days, a girl named Mira climbed the tallest thorn tree to ask the Moon why nothing grew.

The Moon lowered a silver thread and whispered, “Bring me one tear given freely, and I will wake the waters.”

Mira searched among people, beasts, and stones, but all guarded their sorrows. At last she found an old lion lying beside his empty den. “My cubs have gone to the stars,” he said, yet he would not weep for himself. Mira sang to him of their paws in the grass, their warm sleep, their bright eyes. The lion’s heart opened, and one golden tear fell.

Mira carried it up the thorn tree in a clay cup. But the jealous Wind struck the cup, and the tear shattered across the earth. Wherever a drop landed, the dust darkened, split, and sang. Streams leapt from the cracks, joining hands to become rivers.

The Moon placed Mira among the stars, and the lion became the first thunder. That is why, when storms roar and rain falls, children say Mira is pouring memory back into the world again.
